title: Know your margin
principle: Know your margin on every item you sell.

screens.text: Suresh runs a stationery shop near a school. A pen and a notebook both sell for ₹10, but they don't earn him the same.

screens.prompt: Which earns Suresh more: a ₹10 pen or a ₹10 notebook?
screens.why: The pen costs him ₹9, so he keeps ₹1. The notebook costs him ₹7, so he keeps ₹3.

screens.title: Margin
screens.text: Margin is what you keep from one sale: the price minus what the item cost you. Know it for every item.

screens.title: The notebook
screens.text: Price: ₹10. Suresh paid: ₹7. Margin: ₹10 − ₹7 = ₹3 on every notebook he sells.

screens.prompt: A geometry box sells for ₹60. It costs Suresh ₹45. What is his margin?

wrong.b: ₹60 is the price. Take off what the box cost him.
wrong.c: The cost comes off the price. Don't add it.

screens.why: Pen ₹1, eraser ₹1, glue ₹2. Box ₹15, bag ₹80. The price alone does not tell you the margin.

screens.prompt: Today Suresh sold 30 pens (₹1 margin) and 10 notebooks (₹3 margin). Which earned more?
screens.why: 30 × ₹1 = ₹30. 10 × ₹3 = ₹30. Margin times the number sold gives what you keep.

wrong.a: 30 pens at ₹1 each is ₹30. Now work out the notebooks.
wrong.b: 10 notebooks at ₹3 each is ₹30. Now work out the pens.

screens.prompt: This month Suresh's shop sold ₹90,000. Stock, rent and his helper cost ₹78,000. What is his profit?
screens.why: Profit is sales minus every cost: ₹90,000 − ₹78,000 = ₹12,000.

wrong.a: ₹90,000 is his sales. Profit is what is left after costs.
wrong.c: Costs come off the sales. They don't add to it.

screens.text: Margin is the ___ minus the ___ of one item.
screens.why: Price minus cost, for one item. Rent and total sales come into profit, not margin.

screens.setup: You run a small mobile shop. Your ₹150 phone covers cost you ₹90. A supplier offers a new ₹300 earphone.
screens.question: Before you order a box of them, what do you check first?

options.label: How fast earphones sell
options.outcome: They sell fast. But you still don't know what each one leaves you.
options.why: Speed matters, but you skipped the margin.
options.better: Also check price minus cost for each one.

options.label: Nothing. A ₹300 item must earn well
options.outcome: You fill a shelf with them. Later you find each one leaves only ₹30.
options.why: A high price does not mean a high margin.
options.better: Work out price minus cost before you order.

options.label: What it costs me, so I know my margin
options.outcome: It costs ₹270, so you keep ₹30. Each cover keeps you ₹60. You order only a few earphones.
options.why: You knew the margin before you spent money on stock.

summary: Margin is price minus cost, for one item.
A high price does not mean a high margin.
What you keep = margin × number sold.

cards.front: You sell a lunch box for ₹120. It costs you ₹90. What is your margin?
Which has the bigger margin: a ₹500 item or a ₹50 item?
options: You can't tell from the price
cards.back: You can't tell. You need what each one cost you.
